grade.rationale: The runner is readable and builds successfully, but repository-boundary enforcement is incomplete, failures are not isolated by analysis, and extensibility and repeated hashing concerns can produce incorrect or unnecessarily fragile behavior.

summary: The implementation has a clear request/result model and straightforward control flow. The principal risk is that path-scoped analyses receive caller-provided paths without repository containment checks. Additional issues affect failure isolation, classification of custom sensors, hashing efficiency, and deterministic testing. Coverage is unknown; the supplied build analyzer reported no findings, while ESLint was unavailable for an unrelated missing dependency.

grade.rationale: Unvalidated path-scope targets can escape the repository, and review-kind classification is inferred from a hard-coded sensor-name list.
The code is compact, but hard-coded sensor semantics and per-finding file hashing will become increasingly costly to maintain as sensors and result volumes grow.
Naming, immutable contracts, validation flow, and result assembly are generally clear and easy to follow.
An exception from one sensor aborts the entire multi-analysis request without identifying the failed analysis in runner-level context or preserving completed results.
Sensor injection is helpful, but direct clock and filesystem dependencies make timing, hashing, and failure scenarios harder to test deterministically.

findings.title: Path-scoped analyses are not confined to the repository
findings.description: A path-scoped definition is checked only for a non-empty path and is then passed directly to the sensor. An absolute path or a path containing parent traversal can therefore direct a sensor outside RepositoryPath, contrary to the repository-scoped contract and potentially expose unrelated files to external analysis tools.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the requested path against the canonical repository root before invoking a sensor, reject rooted paths when repository-relative paths are required, and verify that the resolved target is the root or a descendant using platform-appropriate path comparison. Consider resolving links as well when strict containment is required.

findings.title: One sensor failure aborts the entire analysis batch
findings.description: The sensor invocation has no runner-level failure boundary. Any non-cancellation exception discards results from analyses that already completed, prevents subsequent analyses from running, and may reach the caller without identifying which named analysis failed.
findings.recommendation: Define an explicit batch-failure policy. For resilient batch execution, catch non-cancellation exceptions per sensor and record a failed or unavailable execution with useful context; otherwise wrap and rethrow with the sensor ID while preserving the original exception. Always allow cancellation exceptions to propagate.

findings.title: Review kind is hard-coded from two sensor IDs
findings.description: Every sensor other than gitleaks and dependencies is classified as code. An injected or future security sensor will consequently emit envelopes with ReviewKind.Code even when its findings are security findings, making the public sensor-injection extension point semantically incorrect.
findings.recommendation: Make review kind part of the sensor contract or finding metadata and use that declared value when constructing the subject. If a fallback is necessary, validate it explicitly rather than inferring semantics from sensor names.

findings.title: File content is rehashed for every finding
findings.description: ToEnvelopeAsync computes the subject hash independently for each finding. When many findings point to the same file, the runner repeatedly opens and hashes identical content, causing avoidable I/O and potentially substantial run-time growth for large files or result sets.
findings.recommendation: Normalize the subject path and cache the hash once per file for the duration of RunAsync, ideally as a dictionary of lazily created tasks so repeated findings share both successful work and cancellation behavior.

findings.title: Direct system-clock access prevents deterministic timestamps
findings.description: Run timestamps are read directly from DateTimeOffset.UtcNow. Tests must assert broad time ranges and cannot reliably verify exact timestamps, elapsed ordering, or clock-related edge cases.
findings.recommendation: Inject a TimeProvider, defaulting to TimeProvider.System, and obtain both timestamps from it. Tests can then use a fixed or controllable provider.
